conventions.convention: Configurations are arbitrary smooth real scalar functions on four-dimensional Minkowski space with metric diag(-1,1,1,1); no field equation is imposed on configurations. Local polynomial functionals have compact smooth coefficient functions and finite jet order.

Balanced derivative variables at field degree r are q_a = p_a − (Σ_b p_b)/r. Constants are separated from positive field degrees. Total derivatives are recovered by differentiating the full coefficient, including remaining field jets, and integration by parts.
Future covectors are defined by metric duality. W has future-null first covector, W − Wᵀ = iE, and W* = Wᵀ. The Feynman null relation is unsigned before its future/past branch condition is imposed.

Scaling uses T_ρ(φ) = ρ^(−d) T(φ(·/ρ)) in relative dimension d = 4(n−1). Independent balanced coefficients admit exact-degree analytic extensions; differentiated descendants and final normalizations obey engineering upper bounds. A vanished punctured derivative coefficient may acquire a contact term.
The transverse product estimate requires factors already defined at the scaling center, nonnegative finite scaling upper bounds, and joint no-cancellation of their wavefront covectors at that center.
Graphs are finite loopless multigraphs with parallel edges allowed. Vertex subgraphs are induced and retain all internal edge multiplicities and derivative labels.
The unitarity S-series uses coefficients (ig/ℏ)^n/n!, whereas the comparison proposition uses normalized S-maps with coefficients 1/n!. Both are coefficientwise formal constructions.
The logarithmic example is Euclidean: C₀(z) = 1/(4π²|z|²). Its scale identity asserts no identification with a Lorentzian boundary-value graph or measured scattering probability.

load_bearing.statement: A scalar time-ordered system consists of symmetric multilinear maps T_n from local polynomial functionals to formal microcausal polynomial functionals, with T₀ = 1, T₁ = id, causal factorization, the specified graph and scaling conditions, representation independence, Poincare covariance and formal unitarity.

Assuming Countable Choice and fixing the stated balanced bases, every off-shell compactly supported local polynomial functional has a unique finite balanced-jet expression, with coefficient support equal to functional support apart from its constant term. Balanced coefficients extend consistently to general jet labels by total differentiation.

Under AC and Countable Choice, distributions already defined near zero with nonnegative finite upper scaling bounds a_j and the stated joint no-cancellation condition at zero have a locally defined product with scaling degree at most Σ_j a_j.

Under AC and Countable Choice, with admissible scalar free data and the stated compatible lower-order translation-invariant extensions, the numerical graph distribution off the total diagonal has a finite upper scaling bound. For a primitive graph the bound is 2|E(Γ)| + Σ_e|α_e|.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix any admissible flat scalar free datum and local scalar polynomial class as defined by the local time-ordered product contract. Then there exists a sequence of symmetric multilinear maps T_n satisfying that contract at every finite perturbative order.

Assuming Countable Choice, two supplied scalar time-ordered systems for the same free data and first-order normalization have a unique formal local, support-preserving, Poincare-covariant map Z(V) = V + O(V²) with S′ = S ∘ Z. Such maps compose and have recursive formal inverses.
For every local polynomial F, smooth configuration φ and r ≥ 1, WF(F^(r)(φ)) is contained in the nonzero conormal bundle of the thin diagonal; consequently F is a polynomial microcausal functional.

concerns.concern: Step 6.1 says, “For a graph let c(X)=X·T_n^1” and “the off-diagonal graph data are Lorentz invariant.” A graph with fixed coordinate derivative labels is generally covariant as part of a multiplet, rather than invariant individually: boosts mix, for example, ∂₀h_F with spatial derivatives. The argument needs to specify the combined action on the finite-dimensional balanced-label space and distribution coefficients, so that c is the equivariance defect in the corresponding finite-dimensional local Hom-module. With that interpretation the cited cocycle lemma applies, but the action and module are left implicit.

The Statement calls Z a formal map “from local polynomial functionals to local polynomial functionals,” while the supplied T_n and the residual defining Z_n carry formal ℏ coefficients. Specify the coefficient ring and formal local-functional codomain, and state coefficientwise extension of T to formal local inputs. This makes S(Z(V)) and recursive composition explicitly typed.

seams_checked.note: The owned definitions and proofs retain the supplied density, future-covector and microcausal conventions. Product and pullback uses require wavefront transversality; singular coincident Feynman products are handled by extension. The transverse estimate checks joint transversality at the full scaling center.

The induction cites precisely the finite-dimensional Lorentz Lie-algebra cocycle splitting result. It does not infer infinite-dimensional or gauge-cohomology vanishing. The implicit label-module construction in its application is recorded as a concern.

The Hopf factorization theorem treats the scalar construction as context and explicitly states that application to actual graphs additionally requires a graph-to-forest interface preserving coproduct, symmetry factors and regularization character.

The anomaly proposition preserves AC, Countable Choice, admissible scalar data and formal-order scope. It expressly assumes anomaly locality, Ward nilpotence and counterterm admissibility separately from the scalar theorem.

The scaling definition supplies both systems and explicitly requires their transported sequences to satisfy the same-free-data scalar contract before invoking comparison uniqueness. It retains Countable Choice and asserts a twisted cocycle law rather than an unconditional subgroup law.
